basis: Inborn disorders of deglycosylation with prominent neurodevelopmental impairment across the recognized subtypes; other organ damage is insufficiently established across the group.
Immunodeficiency with autoimmune cytopenias in ~50%, enteropathy/villous atrophy in ~60%, and chronic lung disease/bronchiectasis in ~60%; endocrine diseases are separately coded.
Renal acidification defect defines the metabolic acidosis; nephrocalcinosis is common. Osteomalacia occurred in only 1/18 patients, below the involvement threshold.
Defined as isolated familial dilated cardiomyopathy; desmin-related ancestry alone does not establish skeletal muscle or neurologic involvement.
Central cognitive impairment of auditory perception despite intact auditory pathways; the definition does not establish ear damage.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability, with seizures in 5/9 patients; both manifestations fall within the neurologic axis.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy; no extraocular involvement is established.
Progressive cerebral astrogliopathy defines the disease; structural scoliosis is reported in 30-79%. Dysphagia and other extracerebral manifestations are minority findings.
The defining congenital abnormalities affect tongue and palate, mandibular development, and ears; functional severity is unspecified.
Malignant embryonal tumor arising in the cerebellum; myogenic differentiation describes tumor histology rather than skeletal muscle involvement.
Cancer occupying a long bone of the lower limb; no other organ involvement is established.
Osteolysis, arthropathy and subcutaneous fibrocollagenous nodules define the spectrum. Cardiovascular abnormalities collectively occur in 30-79%; individual defects are less frequent.
Epithelial tumor of the female reproductive system; reproductive tumor sites have no axis.
Defined by malignant tumor occupation of the eye; the unspecified primary cancer site cannot be assigned an axis.
Alopecia, progressive neurologic disease and pituitary deficiency define ANE. Kyphoscoliosis and contractures affect 80%; dental defects in 60-100% are omitted because of the cap.
Cavernous vascular lesion located in the dermis; both the skin site and vascular tissue define the disease.
Immune-mediated arterial vasculitis confined to one organ. Skin is a common site, but a qualifying frequency across this anatomically varied umbrella is not established.
Joint inflammation defines the umbrella; infectious and autoimmune mechanisms apply only to subsets, alongside degenerative and traumatic causes.
Anaerobic bacterial infection directly involves the lung.
Multiple unerupted secondary teeth occurred in 2/2 patients, establishing an oral developmental abnormality; spermatogenic failure itself has no axis.
B-lymphoblastic blood/marrow neoplasm with an explicitly included lymphoma presentation; no common additional organ damage is established.
Carcinoma arises in the maxillary sinus, included in the airway axis; jaw and digestive-system ancestors do not establish additional tumor sites.
Specific phobia is a purely psychiatric disorder without established damage to an organ axis.
Plasma cell marrow neoplasm with destructive bone lesions in most patients. Renal insufficiency is less frequent than in secretory myeloma and is not established at >=30%.
Peripheral motor neuropathy with defining vocal cord paresis causing persistent laryngeal dysfunction; limb wasting reflects denervation rather than a separate primary myopathy.
